name: Chiangism
summary: Chiangism is the nationalist, Confucian-flavored, anti-communist doctrine of Chiang Kai-shek and the Kuomintang, built on Sun Yat-sen's Three Principles. It holds that a single party should guide the nation under political tutelage, subordinates individual rights to national unity and duty, favors a state-directed economy with land reform and limits on capital, and promotes moral revival through the New Life Movement and later the Chinese Cultural Renaissance.
scope: The mainstream KMT doctrine as shaped by Chiang Kai-shek, from the Nanjing decade (New Life Movement, 1934; China's Destiny, 1943) through martial-law Taiwan (to 1987). It excludes later democratized Pan-Blue politics and Sun's own earlier, more liberal formulations. Evidence is mostly secondary, since the English text of Chiang's writings was not openly available.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Chiangism had no healthcare doctrine; Livelihood stresses welfare and state-led development, but KMT Taiwan built insurance only late, so adherents are split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No minimum-wage position is documented; a state-directed but growth-first economy gives no clear lean either way.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Chiangism favored state direction of the market with state enterprises in key sectors, so it would doubt that free markets beat governments, though private small business was encouraged.

public-ownership.rationale: Sun's Livelihood principle assigns the state key sectors such as communications and mining, and KMT Taiwan kept large state enterprises.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Regulation of capital and land-value taxation limit wealth, but no general stance on taxing the rich is documented; the KMT also courted business.

unions-good.rationale: Under a party-state stressing unity and discipline, independent unions were subordinated; independent labor organizing was restricted under martial law.

property-fundamental.rationale: Livelihood subordinates private property to national interest (capital regulation, land equalization), and Taiwan's land-to-the-tiller program overrode large landowners.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Sun's regulation of capital and limits on corporate monopolies in Taiwan show support for tight state control of big business.

cut-welfare.rationale: Livelihood speaks of providing food, clothing, housing and transport for the people, so cutting welfare as harmful dependency is not its line, though welfare was modest in practice.

worker-ownership.rationale: Chiangism rejected class-war socialism and favored state and small private ownership, not collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The KMT ran secret police and pervasive surveillance in the name of anticommunism during the White Terror.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The New Life Movement preached disciplined moral conduct, and Chiang's regime campaigned against opium; legalization is far from its ethos.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not a concept in the doctrine; the regime censored speech broadly for political reasons, but 'hate speech' protections were not its theme.

strong-leader.rationale: Chiang's regime built a leader-centered one-party state and China's Destiny called for unity under KMT leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Chiangism is a party-state ideology (dang guo) that sees a strong state as essential to national salvation.

limit-guns.rationale: Not documented as a doctrine; a disciplined authoritarian state monopolizing force would restrict private arms (Taiwan's strict gun laws), inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Militarized anticommunist state with martial law and secret police; Chiang prioritized the military and security apparatus.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The New Life Movement promoted Confucian-Christian moral discipline and the regime campaigned against vice.

decide-locally.rationale: Sun and Chiang favored a unitary state with county autonomy only within central party leadership, and centralized authority strongly.

rehabilitation.rationale: The regime used harsh punishment against political and criminal offenders; rehabilitation focus is not documented, so inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: The New Life Movement urged women to be wise wives and good mothers and revived Confucian family morality.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed historically; inferred from socially conservative Confucian-Methodist morality of the movement.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative family ideals and later pronatalist state aims.

more-religion-public.rationale: Chiang was Methodist and the movement blended Confucian ethics with Christian ideas, but state policy was secular-moral, not religious.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Sun's nationalism expected minorities to assimilate into one Zhonghua minzu rather than receive remedial programs; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The New Life Movement assumed gendered family roles as natural, so adherents would not call gender mainly a social construct.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Revival of Confucian virtues and the later Chinese Cultural Renaissance were central, in contrast to Mao's Cultural Revolution.

gradual-change.rationale: Chiangism was a nationalist revolutionary project demanding rapid unification and mobilization, though it prized established tradition; tutelage is staged but directed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration was not a live issue; no documented stance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: China's Destiny stressed national strength and distrust of foreign powers, so a stronger UN is not a core aim, though the ROC was a UN founder.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-imperialist economic nationalism and state-directed development imply protection of national industry, inferred.

nation-first.rationale: China's Destiny centers on national strength and recovery from foreign humiliation above cosmopolitan cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialism and sovereignty emphasis make rights-based intervention unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: A unified Zhonghua minzu nationalism with anti-foreign emphasis rejects open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The regime stressed industrialization and national power; no support for restricting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; a growth-first developmental state would not prioritize drastic climate action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: China's Destiny accepts Western science while rejecting its culture, but no claim that technology solves most problems is documented.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; Taiwan under KMT pursued nuclear power and a developmental state would favor it, inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The KMT was born of revolution (Tongmenghui, Northern Expedition), but Chiangism opposes communist revolution; answer is limited to nationalist revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Sun's distinction of quan (people's sovereignty) and neng (expert government) and the Examination Yuan give experts and tutelage priority.

central-planning.rationale: Chiangism favors state guidance with a private sector and rejects Marxist command economies; it leaned toward authoritarian capitalism after 1955.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets with state or public ownership of key sectors matches Livelihood in part, but the doctrine does not endorse the workers-or-public condition literally.

land-value-tax.rationale: Georgist land equalization with self-declared land value and a tax on increment is a Sun and KMT policy, though not 'most other taxes'.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Livelihood includes an inheritance tax among limits on capital concentration; weak evidence of Chiang emphasis.

basic-income.rationale: Not a Chiangist idea; work and discipline ethos makes unconditional income unlikely.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism and state-directed industrialization favored protecting domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: In Taiwan the state steered the market toward strategic sectors via state enterprises; Livelihood assigns key industry to the state.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land to the tiller and encouragement of small businesses while limiting monopolies promote broad small ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wikipedia says Chiangism opposed communism and that small businesses and state-owned enterprises flourished under its economic model on Taiwan, a money and wage economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state-directed developmental regime relies on a central bank and state finance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: A party-state organizing society into disciplined bodies fits corporatist structure, but such bargaining is not a documented demand.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dang Guo party-state and political tutelage under the KMT, with China's Destiny rejecting other parties' share of power.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The KMT was founded to overthrow the Qing and establish a republic.

democracy-best.rationale: Chiangism treated democracy as a later stage after tutelage and rejected Western liberal forms in China's Destiny, though it nominally endorsed constitutional government.

direct-votes.rationale: Sun's four powers include initiative and referendum in principle, but Chiangist practice restricted voting; adherents would not favor direct votes on major laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils-based power is a Soviet model and Chiangism is militantly anti-communist.

right-to-secede.rationale: Chiangism's irredentism and unified Zhonghua minzu reject secession, including from Tibet, Mongolia and Taiwan independence.

natural-rulers.rationale: Sun's quan/neng division and tutelage by the enlightened vanguard imply some are better fitted to govern.

political-violence-never.rationale: Chiang purged communists in the Shanghai massacre and ran the White Terror.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement prepared citizens for hardship and sacrifice with militarized discipline, though war glorification is not doctrine.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Nationalist state was secular despite Chiang's faith, and the New Life Movement used religion only as moral support; weak evidence.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Laws derived from Sun's Three Principles and constitution, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The party-state monopolizes courts, policing and defense.

military-superiority.rationale: A militarized state aiming to recover the mainland wanted strong forces; superiority over rivals is inferred from the cross-strait rivalry.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Sun's nationalism builds one Zhonghua minzu with minorities assimilating into the Han majority, though framed as a state of the Chinese nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: China's Destiny and the New Life Movement blamed class-war communism and stressed national unity.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Livelihood aims at welfare and equalizing land rights, not equal outcomes; rejects Marxist egalitarianism.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Assimilationist nationalism gives no special land authority to indigenous groups; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Chiangism denounced imperialist wrongs and unequal treaties, but reparations as an international claim are not documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: Chiangism centered on a Chinese nation-state rather than union with other civilizations; Chiang did back Asian independence.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Chiangism rejected individualism and promoted duty and sacrifice.

duties-before-rights.rationale: China's Destiny rejects the Western doctrine of individual rights, and the New Life Movement stressed duty and discipline.

limit-population.rationale: No documented stance; Taiwan later adopted family planning but Chiang earlier favored a large population for national strength.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Chiangism sought industrialization for national defense and strength.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Embrace of Western science in service of the nation is documented, but disruptive acceleration against institutions is not.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; party-guided human authority is the model, inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A surveillance-oriented security state would oppose citizens' uncrackable encryption; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Chiangism combined Confucian restoration with modernization and nationalist progress, so the tradeoff splits.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents hold the Three Principles as the guiding doctrine of the state; ideology precedes results.

direct-action.rationale: A party-state ideology opposes direct action replacing state institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: The regime used authoritarian means for a promised constitutional democracy, rejecting that means must mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Industrialization and national strength were goals.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Marxist distribution principle rejected by anti-communist doctrine.

production-for-use.rationale: Livelihood aims at meeting people's needs but within mixed economy with profit; weak.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory is rejected by Chiangism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Chiangism opposed communism and instead built Dang Guo, a one-party state ruled through the Kuomintang's political tutelage, not through any class.

collective-farming.rationale: Taiwan's land reform created owner-farmers rather than collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Chiangism rejected Leninist imperialism theory as communist doctrine.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state taxes land value and runs state enterprises as part of doctrine.

harm-principle.rationale: The New Life Movement regulated everyday conduct and China's Destiny rejected liberal individual rights.

individual-rights-only.rationale: China's Destiny rejects the liberal doctrine of individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Militarized state with conscription as part of mobilization and discipline.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The regime restricted emigration and the vote is a deferred promise; adherents do not prize exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a moral-national party-state, not a customer-service business; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Livelihood speaks of material welfare but Chiangism treats freedom as subordinate to national unity.

hereditarian-race.rationale: No documented doctrine; Sun's nationalism spoke of blood kinship but not racial hierarchy of abilities.

organic-representation.rationale: Sun's functional-group elements and the party-state's corporatist design give some support; contested.

total-state.rationale: Party-state with the New Life Movement regulating conduct across life, though not fully totalitarian in economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: The New Life Movement and Cultural Renaissance aimed at moral and national revival after humiliation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Irredentist claims (Outer Mongolia, Tuva) existed, yet Chiang also backed Korean independence and did not advocate conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Chiang's rule rested on personal loyalty among followers, but doctrine is modern party-state, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Land to the tiller ended tenancy bondage.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Chiangism claims doctrinal truth in the Three Principles and Confucian virtues.

universal-morality.rationale: Neo-Confucian and Christian virtues were presented as true moral standards, but China's Destiny says Western culture is unsuited to China.

single-common-good.rationale: Party-state unity under one ideology presupposes a single national interest over factional balance.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Chiangist sources never address Zionism; no stance can be inferred from the doctrine, so it is left neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed historically; ROC did encourage overseas Chinese return, but not as doctrine.

revive-national-language.rationale: Mandarin promotion existed but the national language was not lost; not applicable.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Chiangism rejects class-struggle and worker control; firm governance by owners and state.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education was state-directed with a party curriculum; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No documented fiscal doctrine; Taiwan ran conservative budgets but ideology is silent.

economic-freedom.rationale: Chiangism ranked national direction first and held political freedom separate from market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The New Life Movement was aimed at moral reform led by officials, soldiers and students by example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Chiangism backed national independence (Korea, China's unequal treaties), but denied it to groups in China.

force-without-un.rationale: Chiang-era doctrine predates this question and sources are silent; ROC sovereignty emphasis gives no clear lean.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Chiang's Methodism and Confucian ethics treated moral cultivation as guide, not reason alone.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The discipline ethos suggests work requirements, inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: The party-state ideology rejects class warfare and urges national unity.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Chiangism preserved Chinese culture against Maoist destruction.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialism existed but Chiang opposed both Soviet and Western influence and sided with the US during the Cold War.

workers-nation.rationale: Chiangism put nation above class and condemned international communism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The New Life Movement urged wise wives and good mothers though the KMT supported women's suffrage and education.

ban-interest.rationale: No Chiangist support; developmental capitalism uses credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; Sun's nationalism sought one Chinese nation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Zhonghua minzu assimilation of minorities extends by inference to immigrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Sun's design stresses district/county representation and a five-power system; no PR advocacy.

national-mission.rationale: The movement sought national revival at home, not exporting its government abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The movement assumed traditional gender roles as proper rather than an oppressive structure.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Chiangism blamed corruption for moral decline, yet its own regime was accused of cronyism, so adherents split.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The regime justified its security forces' repression as anticommunist necessity.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Kuomintang sought a one-party ideological state that also ran state-owned enterprises and Neo-Confucian moral campaigns, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of Chinese nationalism in this sense; Sun favored assimilation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Confucian hierarchy and rejection of liberal equal rights conflict with nominal equality; split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the doctrine's anti-imperialism concerns China's own treatment, so no clear stance follows.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A unitary nationalism with one law for all citizens fits Sun's unitary state.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Chiang himself was a convert and Christian missions were welcomed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The state schools taught Three Principles and Confucian morality; religion not central.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist-Leninist thesis; anti-communist so no endorsement, though Chiangism favored a strong state in hostile conditions.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Nominally popular sovereignty, but China's Destiny and tutelage reject liberal consent theory.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A militarized party-state does not hold this libertarian principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist competition between nations circulated in KMT thought, but Chiangism emphasised unity.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The KMT banned the CCP and opposition parties under martial law.

separated-powers.rationale: Sun's five-power constitution separates powers but within party leadership.

vanguard-party.rationale: Chiangism has its own vanguard-party (tutelage) but rejects the working-class premise; partial.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Livelihood centers welfare but Chiangism's interests are national.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are a modern British issue; Chiangism has no documented position, and Taiwan's land reform is only distantly related.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were suppressed under the party-state.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources do not link population to poverty; Chiang's era valued a large population for national strength, so no clear lean.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Zhonghua minzu unity ideology views ethnic diversity as a risk for unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sun's Examination Yuan stresses merit selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Martial law and anticommunist emergency rule suspended civil liberties for decades.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The state-directed economy used price controls in scarcity, inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: The KMT controlled media and censored press under martial law.

party-commands-army.rationale: The KMT party-army, with political commissars adopted from the Red Army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Nationalist assimilationism implies cautious citizenship, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; opposes Marxist egalitarianism.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Leninist-influenced KMT demanded party discipline and loyalty.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Strong nationalist sovereignty and distrust of foreign powers.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Chiang held supreme military authority as head of party and state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not addressed; Chiang's Methodist faith is documented but not as state policy on church structure.

clerical-rule.rationale: The doctrine puts party and Three Principles, not clergy, in authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist idea rejected by patriotic anticommunism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The New Life Movement regulated morals and the regime censored publications.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Chiang was repeatedly re-elected by the National Assembly with no term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is one of Sun's four powers in theory but was not practiced.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Taiwan depended on the US alliance.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; the KMT's land policy aimed at tenant-farmer ownership but never banned rental housing, so this is inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The movement drew on rural moral renewal but no explicit claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Recovering the mainland and unification under the ROC were central goals.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Chiangism did blame educated classes for adopting liberalism and communism, but its own elite is educated; split-lean.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: China's Destiny holds Western culture unsuited to China while promoting Chinese cultural superiority.

death-penalty.rationale: The regime used capital punishment widely.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Social conservatism of the New Life Movement implies reluctance, though modern KMT supports gender equality education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Chiang's Methodist faith but the state curriculum was secular and pro-science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The New Life Movement regulated morality.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Blood kinship basis of Zhonghua minzu favors descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Mandarin was made the sole official language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Uniform state authority over religion is inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The New Life Movement issued prescriptions on clothes, etiquette and orderly behaviour with militaristic discipline, a top-down campaign to make conduct conform.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: No documented position on third-world debt; the doctrine is anti-imperialist but sources do not extend this to debt cancellation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-imperialism joined with Livelihood economic reform, but limited.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The constitution was written by party-led National Assembly, but a democratically elected one is not documented as demand.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Tutelage doctrine and martial law-era growth on political restriction.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sources show no stance on a duty of foreign aid; Taiwan received US aid but Chiangism does not state a general principle.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Taiwan covertly pursued nuclear weapons research; weak inference.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The president was chosen by the National Assembly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A state-directed economy keeps the central bank under government.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Wikipedia notes the KMT under Chiang, being anti-separatist, claimed sovereignty over Outer Mongolia and Tuva as well as all of mainland China and Taiwan.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Livelihood subordinates property to national welfare.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Chiangism condemned the USSR but did not use this analysis.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic for a doctrine of the 1930s to 1970s; a growth-first developmental state gives no clear lean.

collective-defense.rationale: Allied with the US, collective defense treaty.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Under Dang Guo the ruling party stood above the state, and Chiang ruled as both Kuomintang leader and President, so the head of state was the party chief.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Chiangism is anti-separatist and claims Outer Mongolia and Tuva, which implies resisting secession, though the sources do not set out a doctrine on using force.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not claimed, though leader cult existed; no divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Livelihood favors progressive burdens on capital.

character-from-environment.rationale: The New Life Movement assumed moral reform through training and environment, inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Party leader's rule above law under martial law; however nominal constitutionalism.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed by the doctrine, so no stance can be inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Sun's five-power constitution is not the classical mix.

leader-cult.rationale: Under Kuomintang rule Sun Yat-sen's thought achieved canonical status as part of an overall cult of personality, and Chiang's own portraits were carried at mass rallies.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not addressed in the sources; no position can be inferred from the doctrine.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land to the tiller redistribution with compensation, a core KMT reform on Taiwan.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the regime's own return-to-the-mainland aim is a related but different claim.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentist claims on Outer Mongolia and territories with Chinese people.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: No Chiangist sources support punishing religious change; Chiang himself was a convert and missions were welcomed, so this is inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: No Chiangist doctrine mandates dress codes of this kind; the New Life Movement regulated conduct but promoted modern hygiene and dress, so inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed; the doctrine's sovereignty emphasis weakly points against it but sources are silent.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the doctrine concerns the Chinese nation-state, not minority emigration strategy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rejected historical materialism for moral and cultural emphasis.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporate monopolies were limited in Taiwan.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not addressed; a state-directed economy would likely intervene, but sources are silent.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; Chiangist courts were subordinate to the party, but a constraint-on-majority debate does not apply to the doctrine.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The KMT advocated a parliamentary quota for women.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Chiangism sought national self-reliance but not shut-off blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine has no documented view on binding trade-agreement standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral cultivation emphasized by the movement but material incentives remained.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The KMT's own military route to power; but anti-communist doctrine of Maoism rejects.

history-own-civilization.rationale: China's Destiny and Cultural Renaissance centered Chinese history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Sun's party tutelage rules citizens, but anti-imperialism rejects colonial tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Wikipedia says education promoted Chinese nationalism based on the Kuomintang's political tutelage, with curricula centred on Chinese history.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a US issue not addressed in Chiangist sources; assimilationist nationalism gives no clear lean.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not addressed in the sources; no stance can be inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Chiangism promoted a regulated capitalism and rejected collapse theory.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A state-directed party-state with Confucian-nationalist morals does not endorse unrestricted private choice of association; inferred, not documented.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional rights existed nominally yet temporary provisions suspended them.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Repeal of unequal treaties was key anti-imperialist aim.

elective-rulers.rationale: Sources describe a tutelage state with National Assembly selection of the president, neither clearly for nor against this general principle, so neutral.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Sun's doctrine includes recall in principle, but Chiangist practice and the stress on obedience leave adherents split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Five-Power Constitution divides authority among five branches and Chiang held party and executive supremacy, so no clean stance; kept neutral.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Confucian-Christian morality gives no clear documented stance.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no stance can be inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Confucian paternal duty of the privileged, inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement mobilized citizens for national purpose.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian analysis is outside the doctrine; sources give no adherent view.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine's concern was nation and Han-majority assimilation, so no documented rule on native-born offices.

party-own-road.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate; Chiangism is anti-communist and has no stance on it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Taiwan accepted US aid and JCRR cooperation.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Chiangism demanded territories lost to foreign powers.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Sources do not address this; scholars debate whether Chiangism itself had fascist features, making any lean contested.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US historiographic dispute with no connection to the doctrine.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not documented; a regime fond of leader monuments would plausibly preserve them, weakly inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no stance can be inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no stance can be inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: China's Destiny holds Western culture other than science unsuited.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army as the party's instrument.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; the New Life Movement's wise-wife-and-good-mother ideal treats care as a family duty, weakly implying no wages.

office-by-exam.rationale: Sun's five-power constitution adds an Examination Yuan to administer civil-service exams, derived from the imperial keju, and Chiangism kept it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism and state control of strategic industry imply blocking foreign purchases, inferred from anti-imperialism.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding delegates removable at will is a council-democratic idea at odds with party discipline and tutelage under the KMT.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not documented; no pension doctrine exists, and a state-directed model weakly implies public schemes.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Taiwan's land to the tiller gave owners title.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; the Legislative Yuan existed on paper but the sources show no stance, so neutral.

single-official-language.rationale: Wikipedia states that under Chiangism Mandarin Chinese became the sole official language on Taiwan.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A modern US legal doctrine absent from the sources; the doctrine's rejection of liberal rights discourse weakly implies disagreement.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no position can be inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the doctrine's sovereignty emphasis weakly points against it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed; Chiangism limits monopolies yet a party-state rather than lobbying shapes policy, so no clear lean.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not documented; a sovereignty-minded party-state would plausibly curb foreign funding, weakly inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not documented; Chiang-era thought valued population for national strength, weakly inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property limits are not addressed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; state direction of the economy gives no clear lean.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; Chiangism's skepticism of Western democracy means it did not rest policy on this theory.

non-intervention.rationale: Its anti-imperialist nationalism rejected foreign interference in China, but the doctrine did not address intervention abroad as a general principle.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: KMT rule kept labour in party-controlled, state-sponsored bodies rather than independent unions; no stand on industrial versus craft form is documented.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The doctrine blamed communists and foreign imperialists rather than an ethnic or religious minority, and claimed the five-races-in-one-nation ideal; inferred from this.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Its Confucian moral revival and New Life Movement upheld family and conventional marriage; abolishing legal marriage runs against this.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from one-party tutelage and martial-law censorship, which put state secrecy and party control above citizen access to records.

local-production.rationale: Its state-directed development favoured national industrialisation and national economic strength, not localism; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: It held that a single disciplined party should lead the nation under tutelage, the opposite of informal trust-based groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Its nationalism fought the unequal treaties and extraterritoriality as infringements of sovereignty; inferred that national law should prevail.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation was defined by Chinese ethnicity and Confucian culture and the doctrine included Chinese of many faiths; Confucian morality is cultural rather than a shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: China's Destiny demanded an end to unequal treaties and China's equal standing among nations, so ritual submission to a leading power is inferred as rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The doctrine is centralist and state-directed, so regional retention of revenue is inferred as disfavoured.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Chiangism kept private property for individuals and regulated capital rather than abolishing it, so common ownership of productive property is inferred as rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Chiangism is defined by anti-communism, from the suppression campaigns to the mainland recovery goal on Taiwan.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Chiangism had no doctrine on who delivers public services; adherents are split.

religion-illusion.rationale: The New Life Movement revived Confucian morality as a basis for the nation, so religion is seen as a moral support, not an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Livelihood favours state-directed development and limits on capital but also industrial growth; adherents are split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The New Life Movement promoted traditional virtues for women and put national duty ahead of equality demands; economic transformation was not its approach.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its Confucian emphasis on family duty, with no programme of public domestic services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Its Mandarin-promotion and cultural revival policies were not framed as a loanword purge; adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Chiang denounced unequal treaties with foreign powers but did not address treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from its anti-communism, which rejected collectivised communes outright.

majority-settlement.rationale: China's Destiny treats minorities as clans of one Chinese nation and promoted frontier development, so settlement is inferred as welcomed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Sun's Three Principles, which Chiangism adopts, were presented as a path distinct from both capitalism and Marxist communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: the ROC grounded its claims to Taiwan, Mongolia and Tibet in China's historical territory, though adherents did not frame it against current residents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: Holocaust denial has no place in the doctrine, and the ROC fought as an ally against the Axis.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine does not address it; Confucian social conservatism pulls one way while Taiwan's law did not clearly criminalise it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: KMT-only rule under tutelage and martial law banned new parties and suppressed opposition in the name of national unity.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the New Life Movement discouraged superstition but the ROC did not make punishing blasphemy a doctrine.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The doctrine is anti-imperialist nationalism, so ruling colonies for a metropole's benefit contradicts its stated principle.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is silent on Islamic jihad doctrine; no lean can be derived.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Chiangism was secular-nationalist and Confucian, so religious law as a test of legitimacy is foreign to it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Political tutelage and party guidance put decisions in the party's hands rather than ordinary people directly.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: Chiangism rejected class struggle in favour of national unity and gave gender equality a limited, traditional shape.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred: the New Life Movement stressed traditional women's roles and the martial-law era had no such recognition.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Confucian moral conservatism and martial-law-era norms; the doctrine never addressed it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: Chiangism claimed to combine nationalism with state-guided livelihood, but adherents were not framed in left-right terms.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: it rejected Marxist class theory as anti-national, so a capitalist-alienation claim is not part of it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: the ROC counted Hui Muslims among the five peoples; the question about Western countries is outside the doctrine.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Three Principles locate sovereignty in the people, with tutelage as a means, not in God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: the ROC had no such rule and did not push secularism against religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine never addressed workplace harassment law.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Livelihood principle combined private enterprise with state direction, land reform and limits on capital.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: A militarised party-state preparing to retake the mainland would not abolish its armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: Livelihood sought equalised wealth, but Taiwan's growth-first policy accepted uneven development.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The ROC aligned with the US in the anti-communist camp during martial-law Taiwan.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Chiang Kai-shek was succeeded by his son Chiang Ching-kuo, but the doctrine rests on party leadership and the Three Principles, not hereditary right, so adherents are split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine wants state-owned banks and state direction of capital, not user-owned mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: nationalist resistance to foreign control pulls one way, but the KMT depended on Western loans and aid, so no clear line.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from Sun's Three Principles, which envisage universal suffrage after tutelage; a wealth qualification is not part of the doctrine.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: the New Life Movement stressed traditional Confucian gender roles and no equivalent critique of domination of nature exists in the doctrine.

reification.rationale: Inferred: this is a Marxist concept, and Chiangism defined itself against Marxism in favour of national solidarity.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: the party-state controlled the press and treated class-conflict critiques as communist, so it would reject this framing.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Formal law codes and a constitution existed, but tutelage and martial law ruled by emergency decree, so adherents are split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Sun's nationalism and the 'five races under one union' ideal sought one Chinese nation including all ethnic groups, not a single-race franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: inferred from the tutelage model, which keeps political participation under party guidance.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: a party-state under martial law did not publish decision records for public tracing.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: Chiangism was secular-nationalist and promoted Confucian morality, with no doctrine of restricting interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: Chiang's KMT used boycotts of foreign (Japanese) goods, but targeting a religious minority's shops conflicts with national-unity ideology.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: political tutelage places decisions with the party and its leadership, not with randomly selected citizens.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the New Life Movement promoted Confucian morality and discouraged religion, but no position on reinterpreting religious law exists.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sun's livelihood principle, which the KMT adopted, called for equalising land rights and restricting private capital to prevent concentration.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the New Life Movement's Confucian moral discipline; the topic was not addressed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The KMT's Confucian revival and Chiang's own Christianity opposed state atheism; the party was anti-communist and anti-Soviet.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A party-state that held power by martial law relied on police and prisons and was committed to suppressing communists.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: China's Destiny rejected power-sharing and called for a single party and unified nation under KMT tutelage.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from state-directed social order and the moral-mobilisation campaigns, which gave the state the lead role.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: Chiang held power for decades under emergency provisions that suspended term limits, and the doctrine favours continuity of leadership.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from tutelage under a single party, which rules out citizen delegation of votes.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A modern question the doctrine never addressed and nothing in its principles settles it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditional Confucian view of women's roles.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the New Life Movement's traditional family and women's roles.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Chiangism's anti-foreign nationalism, as in China's Destiny, makes giving foreigners a political voice unlikely.

rent-control.rationale: KMT land reform capped farm rent at 37.5 percent, so the principle of legal rent caps was accepted; housing is inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state-directed economics and nationalist technology policy.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the New Life Movement's emphasis on discipline and the militarisation of daily life.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents' practice varied with the US alliance.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from its anti-foreign nationalism, though the regime in practice relied on US military support.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Sun's Principle of Livelihood, which Chiang adopted, called for equalising land ownership and limiting private capital.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from a militarist, anti-communist movement that stressed national duty over individual conscience.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: China's Destiny presents the Chinese nation as a single people with a long continuous history, as the embassy despatch records.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the New Life Movement's Confucian, patriarchal view of women's roles.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the New Life Movement's fixed, traditional roles for women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the regime's cult of revolutionary dead; not stated directly in the sources used.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The New Life Movement was a moral revival, but a cosmic good-versus-evil framing is not documented.

culture-before-state.rationale: Tutelage placed building the party-state first, with moral renewal serving it.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; Chiang was Methodist but the doctrine is Confucian.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the New Life Movement's traditional Confucian view of women.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The anti-foreign nationalism recorded in China's Destiny supports Chinese control of China's economy.

independent-unions.rationale: Under KMT party-state and martial law, unions were run under party control, and the ideology placed national unity above independent organisations.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Chiangism was strongly anti-communist and defined socialism through Sun's Livelihood principle under party tutelage; inferred rejection of the workers'-power test.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Livelihood principle and a state-directed economy favour public control of basic utilities; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: The Five-Power constitution has several organs but a second-chamber view is not documented in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Land reform put land in the hands of individual farmers, with state-led industry; community ownership is not a theme.

confederal-coordination.rationale: A unitary nationalist state under a single party left decisions at the centre, and China's Destiny rejects fragmenting localism.

family-wage.rationale: The New Life Movement stressed traditional family roles and the male breadwinner; inferred support for a family wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug-approval speed is not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A martial-law party-state favoured state control of finance; inferred rejection of untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Martial-law Taiwan censored and monitored speech; inferred opposition to anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: China's Destiny rejects liberal individual rights and subordinates the individual to nation and duty.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The New Life Movement promoted moral revival, Confucian virtue and a Christian-influenced ethic as political aims.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A unitary state under a central party leaves regional powers to the centre; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetically engineered crops are not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

dense-cities.rationale: City density is not discussed in the sources, so neutral is the honest answer.

racial-group-interests.rationale: China's Destiny treats the Chinese people as a single nation and opposes divisive group politics.

racial-pride.rationale: Chiang's nationalism celebrated Chinese civilisation and ancestry; pride is inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Chiangism fought a civil war and aimed to retake the mainland, so adherents are split on defensive-only force.

missingStatements.text: The state should lead a campaign to reform citizens' everyday conduct and manners through moral discipline.
missingStatements.rationale: The New Life Movement set nearly 100 rules of daily conduct built on Confucian virtues and discipline.
missingStatements.declined: Partly captured by duties-before-rights, rule-by-example and patriotic-education; too specific to the New Life Movement.

missingStatements.text: Traditional Confucian virtues should be the moral foundation of national education and public life.
missingStatements.rationale: The movement and later Cultural Renaissance rested on revived Confucian virtues such as propriety, righteousness, integrity and shame.
missingStatements.declined: Partly captured by filial-duty, rule-by-example and office-by-exam; too specific to Confucian-revivalist movements.

notes: Sources are secondary or documentary because Chiang's own texts were not available open-access. Many 0 and low answers reflect issues the doctrine never addressed. Scholars debate whether Chiangism was fascist (Wakeman, Clinton) or merely authoritarian nationalist (Gregor).
